source_text: Anthropological analyses further contest the World Health Organization's (WHO) uniform condemnation of all FGC forms, arguing that harm levels differ substantially by type and cultural setting, with milder procedures (e.g., Type I clitoridectomy) often yielding complication rates comparable to or lower than those of male genital cutting in analogous contexts. [39]
